items.title: Portfolio
items.description: This portfolio, built with Vue 3, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS: calm, fast on phones, with a few hidden surprises.
items.challenge: A portfolio that feels like a polished product but stays light: the first version had too many effects and was heavy on phones.
items.solution: A calm rebuild: one accent color, a single blur (the top bar), animations on opacity and transform only, and interactions that make you want to explore.
decisions: Less is faster: I removed glass on cards, SVG filters and continuous animations. The gain was felt right away on phones.
One typeface, one color: Schibsted Grotesk and a burnt orange. Hierarchy comes from size and space, not effects.
WebP images (from ~550 KB to ~70 KB) and brand icons inlined as SVG, with no extra runtime dependency.
All content lives in the translation files: adding a project or a language never touches a component.
highlights: Draggable timeline: the whole journey, from IFCE to today, changes as you slide.
Tags that tell a story: each hobby reveals a line from me.
Command palette (⌘K / Ctrl K) to navigate, switch theme and language or copy the e-mail.
Hidden secrets for those who like to explore.
items.tagline: This site: calm, fast and full of secrets.

items.title: House Pink
items.description: Website and online booking system for my mother's beauty salon: landing page, booking with or without an account, a professional dashboard with schedule, clients and earnings, and video lessons on how to use it all.
items.challenge: The salon booked everything by hand over WhatsApp, with no way to track earnings. The professionals and many clients are not comfortable with technology, so every screen had to be simple and speak the salon's own language.
items.solution: A React site with booking in a few taps, with or without an account, and a dashboard for each professional to manage schedule, clients, services and earnings, on top of Supabase (PostgreSQL with access policies and database functions).
decisions: Rules live in the database, not just on screen: Row Level Security and PostgreSQL functions decide who reads and who books, and an exclusion constraint stops two appointments of the same professional from overlapping, even when two people book at the same moment.
One login for both roles: whether an account is linked to a professional decides if the person lands on the dashboard or on the client account, with no choice screen.
Privacy through access policies: prices only show for signed-in people and each professional's earnings are visible only to her.
Everything can be corrected, with confirmation: undo, delete and remove. A service or client with history is never deleted without warning, so past earnings are not lost.
The same look as the landing page on every screen, designed mobile-first, with 48 px touch targets.
highlights: Booking without an account (just name and WhatsApp) or with one, with slots computed from each professional's schedule, days off and booking window.
Professional dashboard: day and week schedule, clients with spreadsheet import, earnings with period closing, and editing of services, photos and profile.
Lesson center with 21 short narrated videos, with tap circles and captions, generated by an in-house tool from screenshots of the app.
Client account with a greeting, photo, appointment reviews and a feed of the professionals.
items.tagline: Website and online booking for my mother's salon, with a dashboard for the professionals.

items.title: Sinc
items.description: Full-stack finance app for couples: splits expenses, tracks cards, installments, fixed costs and goals, and shows who owes whom. With AI (Gemini), typing "lunch 25 pix" fills in the entry, and expenses can be logged via WhatsApp.
items.challenge: Managing money as a couple means knowing, for every expense, who paid, how to split it and how much each one owes the other. Spreadsheets could not keep up with that routine.
items.solution: A Node.js/Express API with MongoDB and a Vue 3 front end that bring together transactions, cards, installments, goals and fixed expenses, with a balance dashboard for the couple and natural-language entry via Gemini.
decisions: Supabase for authentication only: the API validates the token and keeps a mirror of the user in MongoDB, where all business data lives.
Per-couple isolation (household): every record is stored with its creator's household and queries only return that couple's data, so many couples can share the same database.
Expense splitting modelled in the domain (individual, 50/50 or custom), with backend validation that the partner belongs to the same couple.
Fixed expenses as recurring templates: launching the month creates a real transaction, keeping history faithful to what happened.
highlights: AI-powered entry (Gemini): typing "lunch 25 pix" fills in the form, just confirm it.
Expense logging by WhatsApp message, via the WhatsApp Cloud API.
Dashboard with income vs. expenses, spending by category and who owes whom.
Credit cards, open installments and savings goals with deposits and withdrawals.
items.tagline: Finances for couples, with AI and WhatsApp expense entry.

items.title: My Finances
items.description: Full-stack app for personal financial management.
items.challenge: Excel spreadsheets were no longer sufficient for effective financial control and tracking personal goals.
items.solution: I developed a full-stack application with a NestJS/GraphQL backend and a Vue.js 3 frontend, creating interactive dashboards for visual management.
decisions: GraphQL API with NestJS and Apollo Server, consumed on the front end through Apollo Client.
JWT authentication with Passport.js and an e-mail password reset flow using Nodemailer.
Automated backend routines: generating fixed-expense transactions, closing card statements and reminding about upcoming bills.
highlights: Dashboard with reactive charts and filters by period, category and description.
Credit cards with monthly statements generated and closed automatically.
Savings goals and CSV export of filtered transactions.
items.tagline: Personal finance with dashboards, cards and savings goals.

items.title: Beauty Manager
items.description: Academic application for beauty salon scheduling. The project also included low, medium, and high-fidelity prototypes and an adapted Design System.
items.challenge: My mother's beauty salon struggled with manual scheduling, which caused errors like double bookings or forgotten appointments.
items.solution: I created a scheduling application with a REST API (Python/FastAPI) and a React frontend, allowing clients and administrators to manage schedules.
decisions: REST API in Python/FastAPI separate from the React front end, with ADMIN and CLIENT roles and distinct permissions: admins manage services and professionals, clients book and cancel appointments.
highlights: Built as a pair for the Integrated Project I course at UFC, with 100% of the requirements implemented.
Full UX process: low, mid and high-fidelity prototypes and an adapted Design System.
items.tagline: Booking for a beauty salon, with a FastAPI backend.

story: I started in the integrated technical course in Informatics at IFCE, spent time at a municipal school helping in the innovation rooms, and today I am a mid-level fullstack developer at Cotabox, where I joined as an intern.

I like to understand the cause before proposing a fix, whether it is a critical bug or a slow query. Mentoring people who are just arriving is part of my routine, and when I take on a task I carry it until it is done, tested and live.
I am determined, focused, a bit shy and always studying. Outside of code: video games, pets, coffee, the beach (ideally with coconut water) and family.
